groups.name: Systematic
groups.description: This group encompasses the Systematic namespace from the Prisma schema, which includes core entities for global configuration, business channels, content organization structures (channels, sections, categories), file/attachment management, and associated logs. The database tables in this group are: shopping_mall_ai_backend_system_settings, shopping_mall_ai_backend_channels, shopping_mall_ai_backend_sections, shopping_mall_ai_backend_categories, shopping_mall_ai_backend_channel_category_map, shopping_mall_ai_backend_attachments, shopping_mall_ai_backend_attachment_logs. Key operations include CRUD for each entity, managing business channel hierarchies, mapping categories to channels, file upload and security, and system-level configuration toggles. Table relationships include sections belonging to channels, categories supporting hierarchical nesting, M:N channel-category mappings, and attachment logs referencing attachment operations. Systematic ensures that structural, navigational, and configuration features of the AI shopping mall backend are centrally managed and auditable.

groups.name: Actors
groups.description: The Actors group includes all user, seller, and administrator master entities and their associated sub-records, histories, and authentication relationships. It covers shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers, shopping_mall_ai_backend_customer_addresses, shopping_mall_ai_backend_customer_external_links, shopping_mall_ai_backend_customer_histories, shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers, shopping_mall_ai_backend_seller_business_verifications, shopping_mall_ai_backend_seller_onboardings, shopping_mall_ai_backend_seller_histories, shopping_mall_ai_backend_admins, and shopping_mall_ai_backend_admin_histories. These tables lay the foundation for identity, onboarding, verification, key business role separation, lifecycle, and audit. CRUD, status transitions, external OAuth management, hierarchical address book, onboarding workflow milestones, business documentation, and history/audit trails comprise the main operational scope. There are strong one-to-many relationships from master actors to sub-entities (addresses, histories, onboardings, verifications) and recursive or hierarchical histories to ensure thorough compliance and business process realism.

groups.name: Products
groups.description: This group focuses on the Products namespace in the Prisma schema. It covers all master product records, options, inventory, bundle definitions, product-to-category/channel mapping, tags, search keywords, and extended product content. The primary tables are shopping_mall_ai_backend_products, shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_options, shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_option_stocks, shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_snapshots, shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_category_map, shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_channel_map, shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_tags, shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_search_keywords, shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_bundles, and shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_contents. Main operations include full CRUD for each entity, mapping and managing product hierarchy and visibility, option-level inventory, tags for filtering, AI keyword operations, product content management, and snapshot history. Key relationships include: each product has multiple options, options have one inventory record, products map many-to-many with categories/channels, snapshots give evidentiary/history support, and bundles are managed as specialized product groupings.

groups.name: OrdersCarts
groups.description: The OrdersCarts group covers all transactional entities relating to customer orders and shopping carts. Its schema core includes shopping_mall_ai_backend_orders, shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_items, shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_groups, shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_status_histories, shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_snapshots, shopping_mall_ai_backend_carts, shopping_mall_ai_backend_cart_items, shopping_mall_ai_backend_cart_snapshots, shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_payments, and shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_payment_logs. Operations comprise full CRUD for all entities, order batching and grouping, line-level audit, order/cancellation status trace, full workflow/order history, and both order-/cart-level snapshots for compliance. Carts and orders have one-to-many items, groups batch multiple orders, and both paid and unpaid workflow lifecycles are preserved. This group provides the backbone for checkout, fulfillment, audit, and payment integrations.

groups.name: Coupons
groups.description: The Coupons group encompasses all incentives, promotional credits, and coupon logic. Entities are shopping_mall_ai_backend_coupon_templates, shopping_mall_ai_backend_issued_coupons, shopping_mall_ai_backend_coupon_histories, shopping_mall_ai_backend_coupon_snapshots, shopping_mall_ai_backend_coupon_usages, shopping_mall_ai_backend_points, and shopping_mall_ai_backend_point_histories. The group supports defining coupon templates, managing issuance, redemption workflow, temporal/usage rules, point/mileage wallets, detailed accrual/redemption logs, and audit trail. Entities include hierarchical relationships from template to issues to usages to histories, and each customer can hold various coupons and a single mileage wallet tracked at every change.

groups.name: Coins
groups.description: The Coins group covers the internal/external digital asset wallets, virtual coin flows, and loyalty programs for customers, sellers, and admins. Key tables: shopping_mall_ai_backend_coin_wallets, shopping_mall_ai_backend_coin_transactions, shopping_mall_ai_backend_coin_balances, shopping_mall_ai_backend_coin_snapshots, shopping_mall_ai_backend_mileage_wallets, and shopping_mall_ai_backend_mileage_transactions. Operations span wallet CRUD for 3 actor types, coin and mileage transactions (deposit, withdrawal, earnings, redemptions), order and audit event linkage, real-time balance, and full historical snapshots. Wallets are linked to owners via polymorphic FKs, with cascading effects for transactions/auditing, and tight ties to incentive/financial flows for compliance and reporting.

groups.name: InquiriesReviews
groups.description: This group handles schema entities for all customer-seller product Q&A, reviews, moderation workflows, appeals, and audit evidence. Covered tables: shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_inquiries, shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_reviews, shopping_mall_ai_backend_inquiry_snapshots, shopping_mall_ai_backend_review_snapshots, shopping_mall_ai_backend_moderation_events, and shopping_mall_ai_backend_appeals. Core operations include submitting/viewing product inquiries and reviews, workflow status transitions, AI-based scoring, moderation and dispute event records, and full historical state for compliance. Strong FK relationships exist between customers/products and reviews/inquiries, as well as between moderation events, appeals, and their parent records for robust audit and rollback mechanisms.

groups.name: Favorites
groups.description: This group encompasses all favoriting and bookmark features supporting personalized UX. Database tables: shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_products, shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_inquiries, shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_addresses, shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_snapshots, and shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_notifications. Key CRUD operations cover adding/removing items to favorites (products, inquiries, addresses), retrieval, favorited object state snapshotting for history/audit, and notification event tracking tied to favorite activities. Strong cross-table mappings architect for extensibility, ensuring horizontal and vertical scaling for all future favorites/bookmarks use cases.

groups.name: ContentArticles
groups.description: This group covers the management of site content including articles, BBS posts, news/marketing materials, FAQs, and all related categories, comments, and pin/versioning features. Tables: shopping_mall_ai_backend_articles, shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_categories, shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_comments, shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_pinned, shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_snapshots. Main operations are CRUD for each entity, nesting/hierarchical relationships for categories and threaded comments, pinning/unpinning, revision history, and compliance/audit via snapshotting/archiving. Articles are linked to their categories and can be authored by different account types.

groups.name: ComplianceLogs
groups.description: This group focuses on all platform-wide audit, compliance, security, error, and business rule enforcement logging for regulatory and operational purposes. Tables include shopping_mall_ai_backend_compliance_events, shopping_mall_ai_backend_compliance_snapshots, shopping_mall_ai_backend_business_rules, shopping_mall_ai_backend_access_logs, shopping_mall_ai_backend_security_logs, shopping_mall_ai_backend_system_events, shopping_mall_ai_backend_error_logs, and shopping_mall_ai_backend_audit_logs. Main operations are logging, searching, archiving, and compliance evidence management for business rules, policy changes, security events, errors/exceptions, system incidents, and user/admin/system access. Entities are tightly coupled for timeline integrity and evidence traceability between business/technical operations and regulatory compliance.

operations.specification: Design the authentication API operation for customer registration using the email and password_hash fields in the shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers table. This operation registers a new customer by accepting identity information, and issues initial JWT tokens for immediate login – enabling instant access after sign-up. It is a public endpoint for new-user creation, referencing the email field for identity and password_hash for authentication setup. The API issues JWT token upon success and includes setHeaders, with { Authorization } for client session management. Critical for onboarding and compliance audit histories, registration status (email_verified), and business event triggers (joined_at) are updated through this endpoint. The operation must reference the customer entity creation event for historical and regulatory auditing, including logic for handling duplicate emails.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables customer self-registration as defined in the shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers table. It leverages the unique email field for customer ID, and stores password credentials in password_hash. The service issues a new JWT token upon successful sign-up, using a response body that includes setHeaders for { Authorization: string } per advanced security requirements. Registration triggers joined_at, initial status, email verification state, and associated customer history events for compliant onboarding.

This operation is public, requiring no prior authentication. Business logic requires validation for unique email constraint and secure password hashing, with clear error feedback in violation scenarios. All changes must be audit-logged for compliance as per customer_histories schema.

Upon successful registration, clients receive JWT tokens, are authorized immediately, and all relevant audit, onboarding, and registration steps are automatically triggered. Failure cases (duplicate, validation, security) are handled with precise error codes, and related APIs include signIn, validateToken, and customer profile management.

This operation verifies credentials, issues JWT tokens upon successful authentication, and supports standard login flows. The endpoint uses POST, with email as the identity and password_hash for password checking. It operates with no prior authentication, serving external clients needing customer login. All successful logins trigger last_login_at updates and customer_histories logging. The operation's response body returns the JWT access token and secure session headers. Error handling addresses credential mismatch, inactive status, and locks (status field).
operations.description: Provides customer login/authentication as defined in the shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers table. Accepts email and password credentials, validates against the password_hash, and issues JWT tokens for authenticated API use. The endpoint sets the last_login_at timestamp, updates login event history (customer_histories), and returns tokens in the response. Credentials are checked for validity with business logic enforcing status checks (active, locked, dormant) – with errors returned for unauthorized access. The endpoint is public, uses strong hashing on secret comparison, and enforces unique email for user identity. Related operations include signUp, signOut, and changePassword.

It audits the joined_at, created_at, and updated_at timestamps alongside the seller profile fields. Security is enforced via JWT and proper password hashing mechanisms. This endpoint is critical for the initial onboarding of new sellers and integration with KYC/business verification, as described in the business requirements. Error handling includes duplicate email/business_number detection and validation of all required fields. Registration is a public API with no authentication required. event.review:
Review of 12 admin coupon/point management endpoints including coupon usage update/erase; point wallet CRUD; point wallet history CRUD; and patch/filter/search endpoints. Ops implement soft delete where Prisma supplies deleted_at; admin authorization is correctly present everywhere. Naming uses IShoppingMallAiBackend* with type mapping directly to Prisma tables.

Critical checks: No password or secrets are in any type. All path params are listed and named with camelCase and mapped to proper UUID path segments. For all PATCH (search) endpoints, return type is paginated (IPageI...) as required, never a single object. All PUT/POST follow correct type/intent mapping (update/edit, create, get single, erase) and enforce required params. Logical deletion (where present) is used, not physical. Business constraints (e.g., only certain fields editable, only admin role allowed) are cited in descriptions.

Potential minor area: Some endpoint descriptions could elaborate further on exact immutable/editable field handling for audit. Actual response types depend on DTO shape but there is no evidence of schema nonexistence or misuse. Overall, all listed operations are compliant.
event.plan: No improvements required. All operations meet AutoBE standards.

content.specification: Update a coupon usage record identified by couponUsageId. This operation allows authorized users (e.g., admin) to modify the details of a coupon usage record such as associating it with another order, updating the redemption timestamp, or correcting the associated customer information. Business rules ensure that only permissible fields can be changed after redemption, and historic audit trails must be preserved for compliance. content.specification: This operation creates a new coin balance record for a specific coin wallet. The coin balance entity stores the reconciled balance information associated with a coin wallet, which represents the state after all coin transactions have been replayed for that wallet. This operation is critical for tracking the auditable state of a wallet, enabling snapshot, reconciliation, and real-time balance accuracy within the financial and rewards ecosystem. This API is mapped to the ShoppingMallAiBackendCoinBalances table in the Prisma schema, and is primarily invoked by admin or back-office functions during wallet initialization or on-demand reconciliation.
content.description:
Create a new coin balance tied to a specific coin wallet. This records the currently reconciled balance for the wallet, allowing for up-to-date reporting and audit. The initial balance is usually based on the sum of all transactions for the wallet and is required for performance and compliance querying. Only admin roles are authorized to perform this operation.

This operation writes to the ShoppingMallAiBackendCoinBalances table, which has a unique constraint on the wallet_id field. The request must provide all required information for balance creation, such as wallet_id, balance, and balance_at (point-in-time). Audit fields ensure traceability for regulatory and operational purposes. By using POST, this endpoint distinguishes balance creation from updates, and prevents accidental overwrites.

Audit logs and business rule triggers ensure all state changes are tracked for compliance. Attempting to create a balance for a non-existing wallet or re-creating for an existing one will result in an error. Verification of wallet identity and permission checks are mandatory.
content.summary: Create a new coin wallet balance entry for a specified wallet (ShoppingMallAiBackendCoinBalances).

parameters.name: coinWalletId
parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the target coin wallet to associate this balance with.

requestBody.description: New coin balance creation information for the target wallet.

responseBody.description: The created coin balance record with audit properties.

content.name: create

content.specification: This operation updates an existing coin balance record for a specific coin wallet. The coin balance maintains the latest actual reconciled balance for compliance, fast queries, and transactional integrity. This is mapped to the ShoppingMallAiBackendCoinBalances table and ensures that only authorized updates, such as balance correction, audit adjustments, or manual reconciliation, are allowed. Used predominantly by administrative tools for regulatory, technical, or operational correction, not by regular users.
content.description:
Update the reconciled coin balance for the designated coin wallet and balance entry. This operation allows service admins to adjust the point-in-time balance, update audit fields, or resolve a detected discrepancy between transactional records and wallet balance.

This endpoint writes to ShoppingMallAiBackendCoinBalances, referencing the coinWalletId and coinBalanceId (UUIDs) to ensure correct record selection. Only designated admin roles can update, ensuring no unauthorized modifications. All writes are audit-logged for compliance.

If the target balance record cannot be found, an error is returned; soft deletes are not present in this table. Allows payload validation and triggers system events for audit and re-aggregation.

Errors are triggered when trying to update a balance for non-existing wallet or entry, or when trying to modify immutable audit properties.

This operation is restricted for irreversible administrative actions only. Used if a wallet is disabled, a record needs to be purged, or is incorrect according to audit findings.
content.description:
Deletes the specified coin wallet balance record, identified by coinBalanceId, for the designated coin wallet. As this table uses a hard-delete (no deleted_at), the balance record is permanently erased along with audit context.

This is a compliance-critical operation reserved for admin roles. Any deletion action must trigger a corresponding audit log indicating who, when, and why the removal was performed. The operation checks both coinWalletId and coinBalanceId for identity.

If the record cannot be found, an error is returned. All deletion operations have legal and operational implications.

No response body is returned by this DELETE operation.

operations.specification: Removes a specific comment associated with an article. This operation acts on the shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_comments table, which contains all comments and threaded replies for articles. It is intended for use by admins or authors with proper authorization to enforce moderation, compliance, or handle abuse. When invoked, it performs a hard delete if the comment's deleted_at field does not exist, otherwise sets the deleted_at timestamp to indicate a logical (soft) deletion. No response body is returned. Must enforce comment hierarchy integrity: if child replies exist, deletes them recursively if allowed by business rules, or prevents deletion and returns an error. Related resource: shopping_mall_ai_backend_articles (article master record). Key errors: comment not found, insufficient permissions, child comments exist.
operations.description: Deletes a specific comment for an article, using the commentId and articleId path parameters. The operation will soft delete by setting deleted_at (if field exists per schema), otherwise performs a permanent deletion. Intended for use in content moderation, compliance, or author self-servicing. Handles cascading deletion or prevents deletion if replies exist, depending on business settings. Only authorized users (admin, author) may execute. Error responses provided for not found, forbidden, or child reply existence.
operations.summary: Delete (soft or hard) a comment on an article (shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_comments).

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: ID of the parent article for which the comment is associated.

parameters.name: commentId
parameters.description: ID of the comment to delete.

content.specification: This API endpoint deletes an existing channel-category map by its unique identifier. It operates on the shopping_mall_ai_backend_channel_category_map table, which represents the many-to-many relationship between channels and categories in the platform, controlling dynamic curation and navigation structures. The operation ensures that only authorized admins can perform the removal to maintain business integrity and prevent accidental data loss. Deletion is processed as a hard or soft delete depending on schema field existence, and the system tracks this event for audit and rollback purposes.
content.description:
Deletes a specific record linking a channel and a category from the channel_category_map entity. This operation requires the channelCategoryMapId, which uniquely identifies the mapping to be deleted. Deletion is typically performed as a soft deletion by setting the deleted_at timestamp, as the schema contains this nullable field, but may represent actual removal in some business contexts.

Only admin users with appropriate privileges can perform this deletion, given its impact on catalog presentation and business logic. The operation ensures referential integrity, and changes are reflected in UI navigation, product filtering, and analytics. In cases where the mapping is required for current channel operations or referenced by subordinate entities, dependent checks and warnings should be implemented at the service layer.

Errors are raised if the mapping is not found or the user lacks authorization. The deletion is logged for compliance and traceability, and all changes are audit-trailed for regulatory purposes.
content.summary: Delete a channel-category mapping by its id (soft delete).

parameters.name: channelCategoryMapId
parameters.description: Unique ID of the channel-category mapping to delete.

content.specification: This operation provides a powerful and flexible way to search for and paginate attachment files across all business domains of the shoppingMallAiBackend system using advanced filtering options. It works with the shopping_mall_ai_backend_attachments table, supporting use cases from content management, product asset handling, audit, and compliance tracking. Filters may include owner type, file name, mime type, size, creation time, and more. Pagination, sorting, and keyword-based search enable large-scale operations management, empowering both business and compliance users.
content.description:
Retrieves a paginated and filtered list of attachments in the system. Supports advanced filtering on fields such as owner_type, file_name, mime_type, size, created_at, and more. This operation allows admins or users with sufficient permissions to locate, review, and download files managed as attachments.

Through sophisticated search logic and sorting, users can efficiently manage digital assets, review content for compliance, or perform forensics at audit time. Business rules dictate that only permitted attachments are shown: for example, admins see all, while individual users could be scoped to their own resources.

The operation respects security constraints—sensitive or expired files are omitted unless explicitly authorized. The response delivers paginated results via summary DTO, which includes essential file properties and references for follow-up actions.
content.summary: Paginated, filtered search over the system-wide attachments dataset.

requestBody.description: Attachment search filters and pagination configuration.

responseBody.description: Paginated summary results of matching attachments.

content.name: search

content.specification: Fetches a single attachment's detailed information and metadata by its unique primary key from the shopping_mall_ai_backend_attachments table. Supports business auditing, compliance, download, preview, or management operations. Handles file-level access logic to ensure only authorized users can retrieve metadata. This endpoint is central to file evidence, download, and content review workflows for assets linked to any entity within the system.
content.description:
Retrieves full metadata and business information for a single file/attachment given its unique identifier (attachmentId) from the attachments table. Used for detail screens, download links, auditing, and approval workflows.

Access control is rigorously enforced: only authorized users (self, owner, admin, or privileged roles depending on the file's owner_type) may access attachment details. The payload contains all critical file descriptors, such as storage URI, mime type, file size, hash, owner metadata, and any descriptive context relevant to compliance or business logic.

This operation is also a prerequisite for download, moderation decisions, or linking files to business entities. Unauthorized or non-existent attachment IDs result in an appropriate error response and logging for security.
content.summary: Fetches full metadata and content reference for an attachment by ID.

parameters.name: attachmentId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the attachment file to view.

responseBody.description: Detailed attachment file metadata and business context.

content.name: at

content.specification: Creates a new attachment record in the system, storing all required metadata, reference context, and unique file properties in the shopping_mall_ai_backend_attachments table. The operation supports business uploads from product, admin, compliance, and content flows. Files are first uploaded to storage, then this endpoint is called to record business context. Security and compliance rules apply to owner type, allowed mime types, and retention requirements.
content.description:
Registers a new attachment file in the system after successful physical file upload. Requires all relevant metadata, including owner_id, owner_type, file_name, file_size, mime_type, storage_uri, hash_sha256, upload timestamp, and (optionally) expire_at or business description. The system enforces security and compliance logic regarding allowed file types, size, and target entity associations.

This operation requires appropriate authorization, depending on the owner_type and file linkage context. All fields are validated for correctness and collision (e.g., duplicate hash_sha256 is rejected if already present). Metadata recorded here enables full file management, download, audit, and policy enforcement. Any failure (e.g., integrity mismatch, unauthorized user, invalid owner context, or missing metadata) results in explicit error handling and service log creation. Compliance with file evidence and retention regulations is enforced on insert.
content.summary: Create/register a new attachment record for a business file or asset.

requestBody.description: All metadata about the attachment file to create (after actual file upload).

responseBody.description: Full metadata for the newly created attachment file entity.

content.name: create

content.specification: This operation updates an existing attachment's metadata in the shopping_mall_ai_backend_attachments table, including business context, file description, retention policies, owner transfer, and expiration. Used by business operators or compliance managers to reclassify files, fix data, or change permissions. Does not support updating the physical file contents—use a new record for that. All security, compliance, and integrity constraints enforced.
content.description:
Updates core metadata (not raw file data) for an existing attachment file entity given its unique attachmentId primary key. This supports changing business context such as ownership, expiration, compliance description, or any mutable metadata field as defined in the schema.

The operation requires that the provided fields are valid and permitted by business rules (for example, you cannot transfer to a restricted owner_type without proper authorization, or set an invalid value for retention policy). Attempts to mutate immutable fields (such as storage_uri or hash_sha256) result in an error. All updates are audit-trailed for regulatory compliance.

Errors are thrown for invalid attachmentId, unauthorized access, or business rule violations. Successful updates are reflected immediately in all search results and business logic referencing the attachment.
content.summary: Update business metadata or attributes for an existing attachment by ID.

parameters.name: attachmentId
parameters.description: The unique attachment file identifier to update.

requestBody.description: The fields and metadata to update in the attachment entity.

responseBody.description: The updated full attachment metadata object.

content.name: update

content.specification: Deletes an attachment file record from the business domain, performing a soft deletion via deleted_at update. This operation is permanent in that the record is no longer visible in the UI or business logic, but the physical file retention/deletion is managed by separate storage policy. All deletions are strictly authorized according to owner_type and business context, and are audit-trailed for compliance. This endpoint enforces referential integrity as defined by the platform policies.
content.description:
Performs a soft delete (using deleted_at) of the attachment entity specified by its unique attachmentId. Typically reserved for files that are obsolete, redundant, unauthorized, or found in business error. Business rules require that only the file owner, admin, or privileged compliance users can soft-delete an attachment.

The system ensures that a deleted file cannot be referenced by business entities or accessed via API/UI, except for regulatory/judicial audit with dedicated permissions. All actions are logged for compliance and forensic recovery, and errors are returned if the entity does not exist, is in a critical reference, or the user is not permitted.
content.summary: Soft delete (logical deletion) of an attachment file entity by ID.

parameters.name: attachmentId
parameters.description: ID of the attachment file to logically delete (soft delete).

content.name: erase

content.specification: Enables advanced, paginated search over all logs associated with a specific attachment in the system. Works on top of shopping_mall_ai_backend_attachment_logs, which records every file event (upload, download, delete, access, etc.) for auditing, monitoring, and compliance. Supports filtering by log type, timestamp, and operator. Strict access control ensures logs are visible only to authorized auditors or owners.
content.description:
Returns a filtered, paginated list of attachment log entries for the specified attachmentId. Supports filtering by event_type (upload, download, delete, access, expire), date/time range, operated_by_admin_id, and other business attributes for deep audit and forensic review.

Result is presented in a paginated summary format optimized for compliance UI and operational investigation scenarios. Only users with admin or compliance roles are permitted access, with full audit logging of query history. Results do not include raw file data, only references and event metadata for logs. Errors are returned if the attachmentId is not valid, the user lacks permission, or the filter is malformed.
content.summary: Search logs of file events for a specific attachment (paginated/filterable).

parameters.name: attachmentId
parameters.description: ID of the attachment file whose logs to search.

requestBody.description: Filter and pagination info for attachment log records for specific file.

responseBody.description: Paginated summary of log events for the attachment file.

content.description:
Fetches the detail of a single file event log entry, identified by attachmentId and attachmentLogId together. The log entry includes its event_type, ip_address, operated_by_admin_id, event_context, and precise event timestamp. Access is limited to authorized admins or compliance staff due to the sensitivity of log data.

This operation is essential for detailed file event forensics, compliance incident analysis, and root-cause investigation following system events. Audit and legal review require immutability and evidence-grade access tracking for these records.

parameters.description: ID of the parent attachment for the log entry.

parameters.description: ID of the file log record to fetch (primary key in logs table).

responseBody.description: Detailed audit record for the attachment log entry.

Used to record audit/compliance/operational actions taken by admins or automated processes. Enables comprehensive audit chain for file events. Only privileged users or trusted system automation can call this endpoint. All business rules, context recording, and field validations enforced on entry creation.
content.description:
Creates an audit or operational log record for a given attachmentId, representing a specific event/action taken on a file. Required fields include the event_type (such as upload/download/access), ip_address, and event_at timestamp; optional fields provide context (event_context) or link to the operating admin. content.description:

The operation makes use of the shopping_mall_ai_backend_cart_snapshots table, where each snapshot captures the entire state of a user's shopping cart at a point in time, including all associated cart items, prices, and business context such as status and session token. The snapshot is intended for evidence, compliance, debugging, and customer experience restoration (for example, after checkout, app crash, or customer request). The schema ensures that each snapshot is properly linked to a cart and that all fundamental information about the current cart state is serialized and stored. This endpoint is primarily used after significant cart changes, on checkout, or error events, allowing for full lifecycle traceability. The operation strictly requires a valid cartId and a payload matching the expected snapshot creation schema, including business justification.
operations.description:
Create a new snapshot of a customer's shopping cart in the system. This API operation records an exact, point-in-time copy of the cart's contents, status, customer association, and relevant session context in the shopping_mall_ai_backend_cart_snapshots table. The snapshot acts as key evidence for audits, rollback, incident investigation, and replaying user scenarios. Users, administrators, or compliance systems can invoke this operation after a significant shopping activity—such as checkout, timeout, or detected issue—to preserve all cart details before and after business or system logic changes. 

Security is enforced such that only authenticated users with the "customer" role, and owners of the cart, can create snapshots of their own carts. All snapshot records include full context, rationale (reason for snapshot), and differencing fields for subsequent retrieval, versioning, or rollback scenarios. Related APIs include retrieving cart snapshots, updating snapshots for compliance, and deleting obsolete or erroneous entries. If the cart is not found, or ownership fails validation, the operation will fail with an error. ISellerAuth.AuthResponse.description:
Response object returned upon successful seller authentication (sign in), registration (sign up), or any operation issuing a JWT for a seller. This structure typically includes the authentication JWT token itself, seller identity/role metadata, and may include additional session information for API consumption and client-side storage. The design is focused on security, session management, and RBAC compliance. No sensitive credentials, password hashes, or secrets are ever included.

Fields:
- token: A string (JWT) containing encoded seller authentication and role claims, required for future API requests.
- sellerId: UUID (string) identifying the seller in the system; matches shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers.id; required for scoping session.
- email: Seller's unique email address as defined in shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers.email; used for identity.
- companyName: Seller's business/company name.
- status: Current account status (string, as per status field in sellers schema: e.g., 'active', 'pending', 'suspended', 'withdrawn').

This object does NOT include password or password_hash by security policy.

token.description: JWT authentication token for the seller. Used in HTTP headers for API requests; must be kept confidential and is required for future authentication/authorization checks.

sellerId.description: Unique identifier for the seller in shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers table.

email.description: Seller email address stored as unique identifier in shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers.email.

companyName.description: Registered legal company or business name for the seller; used for audit and display.

status.description: Current account status value (from shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers.status). e.g., 'active', 'pending', 'suspended', 'withdrawn'. See enum in business logic.

ISellerAuth.SignOutResponse.description:
Response object for a successful seller sign-out (logout) operation. Indicates end of JWT session and provides operation status message for the client. Does not include any sensitive information or authentication tokens.

Fields:
- success: Boolean indicating that the logout operation completed successfully.
- message: Optional string (may be null) with a human-readable status confirmation of sign-out.

Intended for consumption by frontend clients to provide user feedback after logging out.

success.description: Indicates whether the logout operation was successful (true on normal sign-out).

oneOf.description: Optional status message to confirm completion of sign out, suitable for UI (e.g., 'Logout successful.'). May be null if not provided.
Optional status message to confirm completion of sign out, suitable for UI (e.g., 'Logout successful.'). May be null if not provided.

message.description: Optional status message to confirm completion of sign out, suitable for UI (e.g., 'Logout successful.'). May be null if not provided.

ISellerAuth.ValidateTokenResponse.description:
Response object for validating a JWT token for seller authentication. Indicates token validity, the current seller profile if valid, and any relevant authentication or role claims. Useful for session checks, UI status, and token renewal logic.

Fields:
- valid: Boolean stating whether the JWT token is valid (signature, expiration, claims, and matching account in backend).
- sellerId: UUID (string) if token is valid; null if not valid.
- email: Email (string) if token is valid; null if not valid.
- status: Seller account status if token is valid; null if not.
- expiresAt: Token expiration timestamp as ISO8601 string if available; null if token is not valid.

Security: Does not expose sensitive information beyond identity. For public/token health check endpoints.

valid.description: True if the provided JWT is valid, active, not expired, and matches a seller account; otherwise false.

oneOf.description: UUID of the authenticated seller if token is valid; otherwise null.
UUID of the authenticated seller if token is valid; otherwise null.

sellerId.description: UUID of the authenticated seller if token is valid; otherwise null.

oneOf.description: Email of the seller if token is valid; otherwise null.
Email of the seller if token is valid; otherwise null.

email.description: Email of the seller if token is valid; otherwise null.

oneOf.description: Account status of the seller profile if token is valid (see shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers.status), otherwise null.
Account status of the seller profile if token is valid (see shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers.status), otherwise null.

status.description: Account status of the seller profile if token is valid (see shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers.status), otherwise null.

oneOf.description: Expiration time of the token as ISO8601 string, or null if token is not valid or expiration unknown.
Expiration time of the token as ISO8601 string, or null if token is not valid or expiration unknown.

expiresAt.description: Expiration time of the token as ISO8601 string, or null if token is not valid or expiration unknown.

ISellerAuth.ChangePassword.description:
Request body for seller password change operation (shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers). Seller must be authenticated. Requires current password for validation and new password for update. Passwords are subject to security policies (minimum length, complexity, etc.).

Fields:
- currentPassword: The seller's existing password (plain text), used to authenticate the update request.
- newPassword: The seller's new password (plain text), which will be securely hashed and saved into shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers.password_hash.

No other fields are accepted. This operation is always audited.

currentPassword.description: The seller's existing password in plain text, used to confirm the user's identity for password change authorization.

newPassword.description: The new password to be set, supplied in plain text. This will be securely hashed internally and stored in password_hash; must meet password policy.

ISellerAuth.ChangePasswordResponse.description:
Response for seller password change operation. Confirms successful password update and provides optional status message for user feedback. No sensitive information is returned.

Fields:
- success: Boolean confirmation that password was updated.
- message: Optional user confirmation note suitable for display (e.g., 'Password updated successfully.'). Null if not set.

On error, appropriate error code will be used by the respective API operation, not in this object.

success.description: Indicates if the password change was completed successfully (true on success).

oneOf.description: Optional detail message confirming the password change outcome; suitable for UI confirmation.
Optional detail message confirming the password change outcome; suitable for UI confirmation.

IShoppingMallAiBackendAppeal.ICreate.description: Data structure representing a request to create a new appeal (objection) to a moderation event in the AI Shopping Mall backend platform. An appeal is a formal objection filed by a user (customer/seller/admin) against a moderation action (block, edit, escalate, etc.) taken on a review or inquiry. This schema ensures compliance, traceability, and business audit requirements for dispute management. Fields reference the appealed moderation event, the appellant's identity, status, and rationale. Each creation is audit-tracked and associated with the correct moderation event.

moderation_event_id.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the moderation event being appealed. References the target moderation event against which the objection is being filed. Required for linkage; determines the subject of the appeal.

appellant_id.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the appellant (customer, seller, or admin) submitting the appeal. This links the appeal to its owner and controls access, business context, and audit.

status.description: The initial status of the appeal (e.g., 'pending', 'under review', 'approved', 'rejected'). Enum values must match business workflow. Required for business process steering, legal compliance, and UI status reflection.

oneOf.description: Optional field for notes or justification attached by the admin/moderator during review/decision. Provides rationale for approval or rejection. Can be null initially, updated by admin on decision.
Optional field for notes or justification attached by the admin/moderator during review/decision. Provides rationale for approval or rejection. Can be null initially, updated by admin on decision.

decision_comment.description: Optional field for notes or justification attached by the admin/moderator during review/decision. Provides rationale for approval or rejection. Can be null initially, updated by admin on decision.

IShoppingMallAiBackendAppeal.IUpdate.description: Schema for updating a submitted appeal (objection) to a moderation event. Only selected fields can be updated (status, decision_comment). Used by authorized actors (admin or the submitting user) to respond to, resolve, or clarify an appeal. Ensures audit/compliance of reasoning behind status changes and final verdict.

status.description: Appeal status (one of: 'pending', 'under review', 'approved', 'rejected', etc.). Updates business workflow and enables decision tracking.

oneOf.description: Rationale or explanation for the appeal decision, set by the reviewer/admin when resolving or updating the record.
Rationale or explanation for the appeal decision, set by the reviewer/admin when resolving or updating the record.

decision_comment.description: Rationale or explanation for the appeal decision, set by the reviewer/admin when resolving or updating the record.

Each property must be comprehensively documented and validated, as these records may be subject to legal or regulatory review.

This structure typically includes the authentication JWT token itself, seller identity/role metadata, and may include additional session information for API consumption and client-side storage. - companyName: Seller's business/company name.
- status: Current account status (string, as per status field in sellers schema: e.g., 'active', 'pending', 'suspended', 'withdrawn').

This object does NOT include password or password_hash by security policy.

## Schema Review Results

### Issues Found by Category

#### 1. Security Violations
- ❌ CRITICAL: ISellerAuth.AuthResponse and ISellerAuth.ValidateTokenResponse include fields referencing roles that may leak more about account status than necessary in generic auth (status field is minimally necessary, but should be checked for excessive personal data).
- ❌ CRITICAL: No password_hash or sensitive data is exposed in responses (GOOD), but response descriptions for ISellerAuth.AuthResponse and ISellerAuth.ValidateTokenResponse should reconfirm that password_hash or secrets are NOT in the schema, even as optional/nullable.

#### 2. Type Safety Issues & Format Specifications
- ❌ HIGH: ISellerAuth.ValidateTokenResponse: All UUID fields as string with format: uuid (confirmed), email with format: email (confirmed), expiresAt as string with format: date-time (confirmed). No types missing.
- ❌ MEDIUM: ISellerAuth.AuthResponse & ValidateTokenResponse: Format is properly noted on fields. All fields are validated.

#### 3. Completeness & Entity Coverage
- ❌ HIGH: Operations reference ISellerAuth.AuthResponse, ISellerAuth.SignOutResponse, ISellerAuth.ValidateTokenResponse, ISellerAuth.ChangePassword, ISellerAuth.ChangePasswordResponse — all are defined and present. All required fields for each are present and align with authentication API needs.
- ✅ No missing required variants for these operations.

#### 4. Quality/Documentation Issues
- ❌ LOW: Documentation for each type is clear, fields are well-described and business context is explained. Descriptions strongly reinforce where sensitive data is omitted.
- ✅ No missing field or property descriptions; all annotated.

### Summary
- No direct security or compliance violations.
- No critical omissions or extra fields.
- Types and required properties are compliant with the operation needs.
- All referenced schemas are present and correct.

## Priority Fixes
- Reconfirm that password_hash or any authentication secrets are NOT ever included in any response schema (even as nullable or optional fields — appears done correctly here).
- Confirm all UUID/email/date-time fields have format annotations (done).

No schema changes needed; all fields and security boundaries meet best practice for auth API.

## Schema Review Results

### Issues Found by Category

#### 1. Structure & Format Issues
- No structural errors detected in core schemas; all properties and types align well with OpenAPI conventions and are well-named for their business context.

#### 2. Coverage Issues
- No missing entity or variant types for the product-channel, tag, and search keyword domains. All variants referenced in standard operations appear to be present (Base, ICreate, IUpdate, IRequest, and IPage variants). However, in a full platform deployment, ensure that similar coverage exists for related objects (e.g., product bundles, contents).

#### 3. Type Safety & Validation
- Format specifications (`uuid`, `date-time`) are present and accurately mapped to business keys and timestamps.
- Enums for ascending/descending sort direction are enforced by `oneOf` const, which is correct. Required constraints are only used for business-necessary fields.
- No openapi-format constraint misapplications were detected for these types.

#### 4. Security Violations
- No security vulnerabilities present. Security boundary is preserved: no response exposures of passwords, secrets, or internal system fields; no request types permitting direct setting of actor IDs for authenticated users (all creations reference product/channel IDs without assignment of owner/actor IDs).
- No sensitive schema-field exposures (like password_hash, refresh_token, or similar) in any response schema.

#### 5. Documentation Issues
- Descriptions are clear, business-contextual, and reference intended domain concepts directly. Field and schema descriptions are detailed, concise, and actionable.
- All descriptions are English and business-context aligned.

## Priority Fixes
No critical issues detected for these schemas. They meet all structure, type, security, and documentation standards as required by AutoBE. No issues requiring correction were found.

If you require a review for another schema group or for the full system scope (including polymorphic relationship types, validation rules for numeric boundaries, or multi-object transactions), please submit the additional schema content for assessment.

IShoppingMallAiBackendOrderPaymentLog.description: Represents an audit or business event log entry for a payment event associated with an order payment. This schema covers lifecycle records linked to payment attempts, results, and business context. Each log entry corresponds to an event (request, response, error, technical or business milestone) in a payment's lifecycle. Important for compliance, forensics, and operational analysis. Every property must directly refer to actual columns or relationships in shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_payment_logs Prisma schema, and all descriptions must reference schema documentation.

id.description: Primary key for the order payment log entry. Uniquely identifies each payment log event/row. Maps to shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_payment_logs.id. Always returned in responses and used as the main entity reference.

order_payment_id.description: Foreign key referencing the associated order payment. Points to the specific payment this log entry refers to. Maps to shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_payment_logs.order_payment_id. Required for linkage and parent/payment event aggregation.

log_type.description: Business or technical type of the payment log event (e.g., 'request', 'response', 'error', 'event'). Used for workflow categorization, analytics, and forensics. Maps to shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_payment_logs.log_type. Only values as defined in the business policy should be present.

log_context.description: Serialized context (JSON/text) containing technical or business information relevant to the event (such as original gateway response, technical trace, error stack, business metadata). Maps to shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_payment_logs.log_context. Optional, may be null if not relevant.

occurred_at.description: Timestamp for when this payment log entry was written. Used for time-sequencing and compliance audit. Maps to shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_payment_logs.occurred_at. Should be in RFC 3339/ISO-8601 format.

All required fields must be present for correct creation.

log_type.description: Business/technical type of this payment log event. Defines what milestone, activity, or event this log entry represents. Acceptable values are 'request', 'response', 'error', or event names defined in the business rule. Must match shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_payment_logs.log_type policy.

log_context.description: Serialization of technical context, request/response data, error/debug stack, or business metadata. Can be plain text or JSON. Maps to shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_payment_logs.log_context. Should capture essential data for forensic, compliance, or debugging review.

## Schema Review Results

### Issues Found by Category

#### 1. Structure & Format Issues
- No structural or format violations detected. All properties are compliant with the expected JSON Schema structure. Properties utilize correct types and nullability, are clearly described, and use explicit `oneOf` for nullable fields.

#### 2. Coverage Issues  
- No missing required variants for the present favorite/appeal modules.
- However, schemas for other referenced types (e.g., IShoppingMallAiBackendFavoriteAddress, IShoppingMallAiBackendFavoriteSnapshot, their create/update/request forms) are not shown here and must exist for the full API (`favoriteAddresses`, `favoriteSnapshots`, etc.). Verify all referenced components exist in the final output set.

#### 3. Type Safety Issues
- All properties use correct primitive and reference types (string w/ uuid format, string/date-time, integer, etc.). Explicit null is accepted via oneOf for appropriate fields.
- Enum/const constraints are present only in descriptions—not enforced via `enum` in the JSON Schema for status fields (e.g., status properties in Appeal schemas). For stricter validation, the allowable values should be enforced via `enum` to prevent accidental value injection.
- Date-time fields correctly use `format: date-time`.

#### 4. Security Violations
- No password, token, or sensitive credential fields are exposed in any response or request type in the reviewed schemas.
- No actor_id/customer_id fields appear in client-facing request schemas except where required for core business logic—these are owner-linked for favorites/appeals for correct RBAC.
- All favorite CRUD operations rely on customer ownership and should be access-controlled in application/business logic.

#### 5. Documentation Issues
- All properties and schemas have English descriptions clearly referencing business logic and domain rules.
- Parent entity relationships (e.g., favorite to customer/product or inquiry) are described; audit and compliance purposes are called out.
- Minor opportunity to leverage `enum` at schema-level for improved self-documenting APIs.

### Summary
- No critical or high-severity issues found in the reviewed schemas.
- All type and structure rules are observed.
- Security boundary for sensitive information is maintained.
- Minor improvement possible by adopting JSON Schema enums on non-nullable status fields (e.g., status in appeal) to prevent injection errors.
- Ensure all referenced types (FavoriteAddress, FavoriteSnapshot, etc.) are present in the generated schema set for full API coverage.

## Schema Review Results

### Issues Found by Category

#### 1. Structure & Format Issues
- No structure or $ref syntax issues noted—schemas are well-formed OpenAPI object definitions.

#### 2. Coverage Issues
- Required variants for pagination, request, create, update, and main entity are present.
- No missing entities for the operations described. However, absence of summary/ISummary and IRequest schemas for some other referenced types cannot be evaluated from this excerpt.

#### 3. Type Safety Issues
- All IDs and reference fields are using the string format: uuid, matching OpenAPI and Prisma conventions.
- All time fields are using format: date-time where required.
- All properties match Prisma field requirements.
- Optional fields accept explicit null — uses oneOf correctly.

#### 4. Security Violations
- No response type exposes passwords, password_hash, or other sensitive fields. All response types are safe, and no request type exposes actor/auth IDs that would violate authentication boundary.

#### 5. Documentation Issues
- Some descriptions are placeholders or boilerplate and may lack detailed business rules, validation constraints, or business context. However, key fields have basic descriptions—could be improved with value examples and more business rationale.

#### 6. Naming and Variant Issues
- Naming matches the Prisma and OpenAPI conventions. All main entities/variants are prefixed with IShoppingMallAiBackend* and match operation naming.
- No forbidden or invented fields appear.

## Priority Fixes
- No immediate critical or high-severity fixes required. The provided schemas are structurally sound, security-safe, and business-aligned for the operations they support.
- For full production readiness: Increase depth and business-specific detail in property descriptions (add example values, explicit business rules per property, and key validation constraints in text to support client/server devs).

No other issues found.

## Schema Review Results

### Issues Found by Category

#### 1. Structure & Format Issues
- No structural errors found. All schemas are proper OpenAPI/JSON Schema objects.

#### 2. Coverage Issues  
- No missing required variants for the coin balances, coin snapshots, or mileage wallets based on the functions presented in prior conversation. All variants referenced in operations are defined.

#### 3. Type Safety Issues
- All date/time fields use format: 'date-time' and are correct.
- UUIDs are correctly specified as 'string' with 'format: uuid'.
- Monetary fields use 'number' (for amounts and balances) as required.
- Properties supporting null have explicit oneOf (string or null), which is compliant.

#### 4. Security Violations
- No password, token, or hash fields are present in any response or request type. No actor ID in requests (only allowed in output as IDs, not as user-supplied input).
- No ownership mutation or permission escalation fields.

#### 5. Documentation Issues
- Descriptions are comprehensive, referencing business context, and constraints are documented. Field-by-field documentation is clear and aligns with business rules.

---
## Priority Fixes
- No security or critical functional issues found.
- No type or business logic mapping problems detected.
- No missing required entities/variants.
- Descriptions and formats are business-appropriate.
- Null handling is explicit and valid.
- No forbidden properties or missing required properties.

## Possible Minor Improvements
- None necessary at this time. Schemas are well-documented and comply with AutoBE/Prisma/OpenAPI standards.

If business logic domain expands, ensure: (a) nullability stays explicit, (b) enums are added if any fields get closed value sets, and (c) future variants adhere to the established format/naming pattern.

## Overall Assessment
No issues found. All schemas are well-structured, secure, and fully compliant with business and audit requirements. Ready for production and immediate use.

## Schema Review Results

### Issues Found by Category

#### 1. Security Violations
- ❌ CRITICAL: Several response schemas may leak sensitive identity (IDs) and status information (e.g., adminId, sellerId, setHeaders) directly, which while often acceptable, must be explicitly verified against security requirements regarding exposure of unique identifiers. Token responses correctly avoid leaking passwords or hashes.

#### 2. Coverage Issues
- ❌ HIGH: Only a subset of necessary operation schemas is provided: e.g., only customer/admin/seller auth schemas and some password change schemas, while referenced types like ICustomerSignUp.Request, ICustomerChangePassword.Request, ICustomerSignIn.Request, etc., are not included here. (This may be a sampling issue or out of scope for the sample shown, but all referenced types by endpoints must exist.)
- ❌ HIGH: Variants for IUpdate, ISummary, IRequest for some schemas are missing; operation endpoints expect these, such as for update, search, and summary listings.

#### 3. Type Safety Issues
- ❌ MEDIUM: setHeaders in sign-up/sign-in responses is modeled as an object with just Authorization (string), but should document that only enums/const or specific header patterns are permitted. Email fields are marked as format: email, but other UUID and date fields should be format-annotated everywhere.
- ❌ MEDIUM: Password fields are included only in request bodies (correct), but in some schemas, descriptions don’t explicitly reaffirm that any server-side storage is hashed (for password_hash) per security best practice.

#### 4. Documentation Issues
- ❌ LOW: Descriptions are generally strong and pragmatic, but a few are inconsistent in tense/style or do not reiterate security policy enough (e.g., which fields are ever returned to the client). Some descriptions, particularly those for setHeaders and status/message fields, could be improved for clarity on business error/success states.
- ❌ LOW: Enum/const values for status fields (e.g., admin status, seller status) are not exhaustively listed—should enumerate possible values to guide implementers.

## Priority Fixes
1. Ensure all referenced schemas (ICustomerSignUp.Request, ICustomerChangePassword.Request, etc.) are present and defined with full required fields (CRITICAL/HIGH).
2. Remove any server-only or sensitive fields from all responses unless business and compliance rules allow (CRITICAL).
3. Add enum values for all status and role fields, and specify explicit allowed values (HIGH/MEDIUM).
4. Ensure all UUID and date fields use 'format: uuid' and 'format: date-time' where relevant (MEDIUM).
5. Clarify and enforce that password fields are never present in responses, and storage is always hashed (LOW/doc).
6. Update descriptions for consistency and clarify field purposes and security behaviors (LOW).

## If no issues are found, simply state 'No issues found.'

## Schema Review Results

### Issues Found by Category

#### 1. Structure & Format Issues
- No structural errors detected. Schemas follow object definitions and $ref usage is correct.

#### 2. Coverage Issues  
- Missing several referenced entity variants:
    - Required interfaces such as `IShoppingMallAiBackendOrderGroup.ISummary`, `IPageIShoppingMallAiBackendOrderStatusHistory.ISummary`, `IShoppingMallAiBackendOrderSnapshot.ICreate`, `IShoppingMallAiBackendOrderSnapshot.IUpdate`, and list collection/summary schemas referenced in operations are not provided here. For production readiness, all DTOs referenced in the OpenAPI operation list must be present as schema variants (e.g., ISummary for data pagination, ICreate/IUpdate for each main entity).
    - The base object for paginated result sets (like `IPageIShoppingMallAiBackendOrderStatusHistory`) is given, but the ISummary variants for row objects are not (needed for proper API docs and SDK typing).
    - Pagination object `IPage.IPagination` is present and correct.

#### 3. Type Safety Issues
- Mixed use of `oneOf` for nullable string fields: the convention is valid, but using `type: ['string', 'null']` would be more typical for succinctness and compatibility with OpenAPI tooling.
- Format specifications (`format: uuid`, `format: date-time`) are accurately set where needed.
- Any enums/consts or business status fields do not have enumerations set; where these are bound to business constants, `enum` values should be added (e.g., for order status or actor type).

#### 4. Security Violations
- ⚠️ No critical security exposures detected for these schemas (no sensitive internal fields, passwords, tokens, or actor IDs in requests/responses).
- In context, `actor_id` is audit/provenance and not end-user input.

#### 5. Documentation Issues
- Some descriptions are generic. Deeper references to the underlying business logic or Prisma model comments can improve usability (e.g., clarify what values are allowed for status fields, business meanings of context fields, and examples).

## Priority Fixes
1. Add all missing schema variants for each DTO referenced in the API operation list (especially ISummary, ICreate, IUpdate types for every main entity used in paginated endpoints)
2. Where possible, add `enum` values to status and actor fields (where business logic defines a fixed set of strings).
3. Improve property descriptions to reflect actual business rules, constraints, and linkages to the source Prisma schema fields and requirement documentation.
4. Standardize nullable property schemas to `type: ["string", "null"]` instead of using `oneOf` for clearer OpenAPI output (optional but preferred for compatibility).

If no new variants or corrections are applied, APIs expecting these DTOs will fail serialization or validation and code generation will be incomplete.

## Schema Review Results

### Issues Found by Category

#### 1. Structure & Format Issues
- No structural JSON issues present. All schemas follow the expected OpenAPI/JSON schema structure. 

#### 2. Coverage Issues
- No critical entity or variant is missing for the APIs presented in this batch; all referenced DTOs have matching detailed, create, update, and summary variants as needed. Schemas exist for complex pagination (IPage), request (IRequest), summary (ISummary), and update DTOs. All necessary core objects for order and orderItem management are properly covered.

#### 3. Type Safety Issues
- All field types conform to expected types and formats from the Prisma schema:
  - UUID fields have format: "uuid".
  - Datetime fields have format: "date-time".
  - Nullable fields (such as note, deleted_at, order_group_id) are modeled using oneOf: [string, null]; explicit null support is proper.
  - No violations around primitive vs. object properties or array typing.
  - Currency fields and other string-typed enums are simply "string"; if more enum constraints are required, this is manageable but not a blocking issue as per this API contract.

#### 4. Security Violations
- No passwords, password_hash, or sensitive authentication fields are included in response models. 
- No actor ID leak in public-facing request schemas—only contextual IDs such as "customer_id" are used and are necessary per domain logic (never for authentication boundary crossing).
- All server-side managed fields (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, id, etc.) are only output in main entity/summary/ad-hoc retrievals and not present in creation/update DTOs.
- Request and update schemas do NOT accept system-generated immutable fields (no id, created_at, etc.).
- All actor boundaries appear preserved.

#### 5. Documentation Issues
- Descriptions for all properties are present, clear, give business context, and appropriately reference format or domain requirements.
- Required vs. optional fields are clearly specified via "required" array and property type.
- Documentation is in English, matches business use, and guides API consumers regarding constraints, NULL handling, and usage.

### Overall
No critical, high, or medium-severity issues detected in this schema batch. Coverage is complete for the shown API set, and type mapping aligns with the underlying Prisma schema and business logic. Documentation and format guides are consistent. 

## Priority Fixes
None—no security, completeness, or accuracy-related changes required.

## Schema Review Results

### Issues Found by Category

#### 1. Security Violations
- ❌ CRITICAL: `IShoppingMallAiBackendCustomer` includes the `password_hash` field as required and in type output schemas. This is a direct security vulnerability: password hashes must never be exposed in API responses. Although the schema notes "not exposed in responses" in the description, its presence as a required property in the core entity makes it easy to accidentally include it in responses—this should be omitted from all response/output-only schemas.

#### 2. Variant/Completeness Issues
- ❌ HIGH: The schemas for paginated listings rely on `IShoppingMallAiBackendCustomer.ISummary`, but other essential variants required for full operational coverage (such as `ICreate`, `ISummary`, `IUpdate` for related entities like addresses, external links, and history) are not all shown or covered. If they are missing from the registry, this will impact completeness.
- ❌ HIGH: No request/response variants for create operations, such as `IShoppingMallAiBackendCustomer.ICreate` or similar for addresses/external links/histories—critical for POST endpoints.

#### 3. Type/Field Issues
- ❌ HIGH: `IShoppingMallAiBackendCustomer` has password_hash as a required field, but registration/login/change password flows should handle the password as a credential, not as a property on the main entity.
- ❌ MEDIUM: Some date-time fields allow null but descriptions are ambiguous as to when null is valid or should be supported (e.g., last_login_at, deleted_at); update descriptions for business clarity.
- ❌ MEDIUM: Use of `oneOf: [string, null]` is correct for optional datetimes and nullable fields, but ensure this pattern is consistent in all related schemas for compatibility.

#### 4. Documentation Issues
- ❌ LOW: Some descriptions are verbose or duplicated, leading to potential confusion about business meaning (e.g., multiple times "User-defined short name or description for this address (can be null)" for alias).

## Priority Fixes
1. **CRITICAL**: Remove password_hash from any schema variant used for API responses or as an output schema. Keep password_hash only for internal/server-side use and ICreate request structures where the password is being supplied (and never returned in a response).
2. **HIGH**: Ensure all request and response DTO variants exist, including all CRUD use cases—especially ICreate variants for customers, addresses, links, histories, etc. Add ISummary, IUpdate, and ICreate for all main entities as needed.
3. **HIGH**: Revise required field lists for each schema so that required/optional aligns with the business logic and Prisma nullable definitions. E.g., password_hash not required for updates, never in summaries or responses.
4. **MEDIUM**: Standardize nullable date/datetime usage and update descriptions for clarity—document when null values are valid and under what states.
5. **LOW**: Clean up redundant or overly verbose descriptions.

## Overall
- No system-generated fields (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) should be accepted on requests—should only be included in responses.
- No authentication or actor ID (user_id, customer_id) should be accepted in create/update requests—should always come from the auth context.
- Update patterns (all fields optional, no business invariants like email/nickname changes for existing users unless allowed).
- Business logic must ensure password hashing and validation is detached from the main customer entity.

## Schema Review Results

### Issues Found by Category

#### 1. Security Violations
- ❌ No critical security violations found. All sensitive fields (hashed passwords) are not present in response schemas. No actor ID is accepted in a request in a way that would breach authentication boundaries. 

#### 2. Coverage Issues
- ❌ No issues found. All referenced operations for point and coin wallet/transaction management have matching schema types present. No missing schemas or entity definitions detected in the subset reviewed.

#### 3. Type Safety & Format Issues
- ❌ Positive: All UUIDs have correct format: "uuid". Numbers have double or integer format when needed. Date/time fields have "date-time" as required.  
- ❌ Nullability: All fields which are nullable are consistently present as oneOf with null option, as best practice.

#### 4. Completeness & Variants
- ❌ No missing create/update variants for these business objects. (All ICreate/IUpdate present as referenced.)

#### 5. Documentation & Consistency
- Minor inconsistencies in property naming between schemas for requests and entities (e.g., 'remarks' and 'transaction_reason' serve similar purposes, but this reflects underlying business concepts). All object and property descriptions are adequate, referencing business logic or audit requirements from requirements analysis.

#### 6. Discriminator Issues
- Not applicable for this schema set (no explicit discriminators in usage or union types).

---
## Summary
- No critical, high, or medium issues were found in the provided schema set. All properties, types, and required fields match the referenced endpoints and business expectations. The schemas follow the OpenAPI and business specification—UUIDs, date-times, nullability, numeric precision, and documentation are handled as per best practices. No security or completeness violations present.


## Priority Fixes
- No blocking issues. No changes required. (If user has downstream schemas or wants harmonization of note/remark fields, could consider convention alignment across all business types, but not required for compliance, quality, or security.)

## Schema Review Results

### Issues Found by Category

#### 1. Structure & Format Issues
- No structure issues detected (all referenced schemas are present, properly required fields set, oneOf used for nullable fields, formats used for uuid and date-time).

#### 2. Coverage Issues  
- HIGH: Only the IShoppingMallAiBackendMileageWallet and IShoppingMallAiBackendMileageTransaction domain entities are included. Schemas for related entities (such as IShoppingMallAiBackendFavoriteProduct, IShoppingMallAiBackendFavoriteInquiry, etc., referenced in the OpenAPI spec) are missing—full variant coverage for the operation list is lacking.
- HIGH: No ISummary schema variants or paginated result ISummary schemas for IShoppingMallAiBackendMileageWallet present, which are referenced in endpoints for pagination.
- HIGH: Missing ISummary variants, IRequest, ICreate, IUpdate variants for all other endpoints described in the OpenAPI operation list (e.g., product inquiries, favorite modules, etc.).

#### 3. Type Safety Issues
- No type mapping issues in the provided schemas (uuid and date-time used where required).
- The use of oneOf for nullable fields is correct.

#### 4. Security Violations
- No forbidden security exposure found (no password or sensitive credential returned in responses).
- No actor IDs are accepted directly in create/update requests that would violate authentication context in these schemas. However, the customer_id field is present in requests; proper auth boundary must be enforced at the handler level.

#### 5. Documentation Issues
- Some property descriptions are overly generic and could more strongly align with domain use or include business rule/constraint references where applicable.

## Priority Fixes
1. **Add all missing entities and variants** referenced in the OpenAPI operation list (CRITICAL for schema completeness):
   - IShoppingMallAiBackendFavoriteProduct, IShoppingMallAiBackendFavoriteInquiry, IShoppingMallAiBackendProductReview, IShoppingMallAiBackendFavoriteAddress, and their corresponding IRequest, ISummary, ICreate, IUpdate schemas.
   - Add missing ISummary and IRequest schemas for each business object presented in the OpenAPI spec.
2. **Add paginated result schemas** (e.g., IPageIShoppingMallAiBackendMileageWallet, IPageIShoppingMallAiBackendFavoriteProduct, etc.) for each domain referenced in paging endpoints.
3. Improve documentation for each property to provide concise descriptions that reference the business requirement or logic (recommend referencing Prisma property documentation or table comments for precision and authoritativeness).
4. Ensure all request types which should not accept actor identity fields (customer_id, etc.) exclude those fields as input. If the system already pulls actor_id from authentication context, adjust schemas accordingly.

## If No Issues
No issues found.

Add schemas for all missing entities referenced in OpenAPI operations: IShoppingMallAiBackendFavoriteProduct, IShoppingMallAiBackendFavoriteInquiry, IShoppingMallAiBackendFavoriteAddress, IShoppingMallAiBackendProductReview, and variants (IRequest, ISummary, ICreate, IUpdate) and relevant paginated/page types for each.

- 3. For each type referenced as a request or response body in the OpenAPI, add ISummary variants as needed.

- Confirm that any actor ID fields (e.g., customer_id) in ICreate/IUpdate requests are only present when business logic allows and are NOT required when the authenticated user context must be used instead (actor assignment via authentication context, not client input).
- Confirm that no 'password', 'password_hash', or other credential fields are present in response objects.

### Documentation & Style
- Add schema property descriptions, referencing business requirement, data source, and constraints (reference Prisma property docstrings for alignment).
- Improve schema variant documentation to highlight which endpoints consume or produce which variant.

### Validation Improvements
- For all UUID fields, set 'format: uuid'.
- For all ISO timestamp fields, set 'format: date-time'.
- Use oneOf with null for all optional fields with possible null values.
- Ensure enum/consts are used for fields with fixed business values if that constraint can be determined from requirements or OpenAPI spec.

No improvements required. All schemas meet AutoBE standards.

#### 1. Structure & Format Issues
- No structure errors found; all schemas are valid OpenAPI types and are named.

- No missing referenced schemas in this snippet; all referenced types (in requestBody/responseBody) are present.

#### 3. Type Safety Issues
- No explicit type mapping errors found. All uuid/date-time formats are typed with appropriate "format" property. Nullability for optional fields is handled with oneOf as required.

#### 4. Security Violations
- No CRITICAL security violations observed. 
  - No password, refresh token, or secret fields exposed in responses.
  - No actor_id/ownership fields are present in request variant types except for expected polymorphic owners (used for resource-based security, not as identity injection).
  - All request types are for filtering/search or for attachment creation/updates and refer only to business keys.

#### 5. Documentation Issues
- Property and schema descriptions are generally strong, referencing both technical and business context from ERD/Prisma.
- No direct references to business rules or advanced validation in property descriptions, but type and intent are clear.
